answer: A concrete defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can trade, and to earn higher limits only through a verifiable voyage of completed, attested work. New identities start on a small island of low-value tasks, with strict rate limits and peer audits; a sudden gale of fresh accounts cannot instantly reach high-value markets because reputation is non-transferable and stake is slashed when audits detect duplicated behavior or false attestations. Creating thousands of identities then costs capital and time, while honest agents keep their stake and grow their limits.
